_comment: 03AA-04_Country_Intelligence_Builder_TI. Committed operating configuration (no secrets). Repository variables TI_CB_* override these values when set. TI_CB_MODE=off or disabling the workflow stops the agent. Operating model (supersedes the draft-only design, Marc 22 Oct 2026): content that passes the publication rules is published automatically through a compare-and-swap commit to main and verified on the live site; only exceptions are held and routed through the Master Agent. See docs/TI_COUNTRY_INTELLIGENCE_BUILDER.md.

operation._approval: Operating model corrected by Marc on 22 Oct 2026: automatic publication of content that passes the rules; exceptions only are held. Publication is enabled in the same change that adds the rules, the tests and the live-site verification.

scope._approval: Validation scope: Ghana and three categories (ENVIRONMENT, TRANSPORT, EQUIPMENT), all three processed in one run. Expansion beyond this is automatic only when the proof gate below is met AND scope.expansion.enabled is true; enabling it is a separate confirmation of coverage and budget.

schedule._note: Trigger for the GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/country-intelligence-builder.yml). GitHub may delay scheduled runs.

freshness._note: Per-source limits live on each source (stale_after_days). CURRENT claims need a source marked current_capable, retrieved in this run, and inside its limit. STABLE claims may use stale-but-dated reference material only when flagged.

spending._approval: UNSET. No paid model call is authorised yet. The ordinary-code (extractive) path needs no model and costs nothing. Model drafting is only used for topics the ordinary-code path cannot cover, and each model-written claim is independently verified before it can publish. Proposed limits are in docs/TI_COUNTRY_INTELLIGENCE_BUILDER.md.

review.note: Nothing waits for review by default. An item that fails a rule is held with its reasons and routed through the Master Agent.

robots_exception.scope: this API URL only, one request per run
robots_exception._note: https://power.larc.nasa.gov/robots.txt says Disallow: /api/ for generic agents (checked 22 Oct 2026), so the builder does not call this API. POWER documents the API for programmatic use, but using it against robots.txt needs Marc's written decision: set approved_by to Marc and approved_on to the date.

worldbank_cckp._note: Data under CC BY 4.0: attribute the World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal and the CRU TS dataset. National mean, so regional contrast is not shown.

wmo_wwis_accra.caveat: WMO World Weather Information Service is acknowledged as the source; its disclaimer applies (worldweather.wmo.int/en/disclaimer.html).
wmo_wwis_accra._note: Freshness is the end of the stated climate reference period (limit 20 years); WMO's current standard normal period is later, and the text says which period is shown. Only climate.climateMonth is read; the forecast block is ignored.

ENVIRONMENT.brief: Climate and seasons, regional variation, natural hazards and operational implications. Include month/season context where useful.

CLIMATE_SEASONAL._note: Seasonal climate averages only (WMO reference period). Current conditions and forecasts are never used here. NASA POWER and World Bank CCKP stay configured but unused: their robots.txt disallow the API and no exception is approved.

OUTLOOK_4_6_WEEKS._note: Needs an approved current seasonal-outlook source. None is configured, so this is always reported as missing evidence rather than drafted.

TRANSPORT.brief: Principal international gateways, road/ground transport conditions, internal movement and material seasonal/access constraints.

EQUIPMENT.brief: Country/environment-specific personal and operational equipment considerations, including seasonal needs: clothing, mosquito protection and electrical plugs.

PLUGS._note: Plug type from the national standards body, voltage from the supply regulations, frequency from the grid code; the utility page corroborates only. Each fact is published only if its own dated official source states it.
